newsitem.title: USA: Ag is important issue in China/WTO accession - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Ag is important issue in China/WTO accession - USDA.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman denied Wednesday that agricultural concerns are being ignored in discussion over allowing China into the World Trade Organization.

Speaking at the National Press Club, Glickman disagreed with claims by some in the agricultural community that the administration is giving short shrift to worries that China is not opening its markets enough to U.S. agricultural products.
"We're not getting rolled by anybody," in the China/WTO issue, Glickman said in response to questions.

Glickman said he was present at meetings between President Clinton and Chinese leaders at the APEC conference in Manila last year, and that agriculture "took up a big portion of the debate." Clinton stood up solidly for U.S. agriculture, Glickman said.
"The president specifically said the trends towards Chinese purchases of U.S. agricultural products were not good, and he wanted to see that changed," the secretary said.

Glickman said that Clinton has made it clear that the opening of Chinese markets and honoring international standards in sanitary and phytosanitary issues "are things that the Chinese have to do -- among other things -- in order to gain (WTO) accession."
